title: Thirty Minor Upanishads
attributionNote: The Upanishads are anonymous and belong to different Vedic schools; several of the texts here are sectarian and late, and their attribution to particular schools is traditional rather than historical.
description: This collection gathers thirty shorter Upanishads, most of them concerned with yoga, renunciation and the disciplines of the ascetic life: the Mahanarayana and the Yogakundalini, the Amritabindu and the Dhyanabindu, the Sandilya and the Varaha, the Rama-tapaniya and the Narayana. Some are brief meditations on the syllable Om or the self; others are manuals of breath, posture and the inner sound. Together they show the range of the later Upanishadic literature beyond the twelve or thirteen principal texts.
historicalContext: The minor Upanishads were composed over many centuries, most of them after the principal Upanishads and some as late as the medieval period; they belong to the Atharva, Yajur, Sama and Rigvedic schools. K. Narayanasvami Aiyar's English translation was published in 1914 and is the standard public-domain collection of these texts.
availabilityNote: Complete. All thirty Upanishads of Aiyar's collection are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one Upanishad per chapter. The volume's title page, contents and index of proper names are not part of the work.
